aria: Animated recap of the Lakers' 124 to 114 road win at Atlanta: Luka Dončić's drive with 2:27 left, quarter-by-quarter scoring, his 32 points and 10 assists, the top scorers, how the Lakers won, and the next game at Milwaukee.
notes: Box score from the Lakers' 124–114 win over the Atlanta Hawks in Atlanta on Nov 9, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, with game details from the AP (via Yahoo Sports and the Killeen Daily Herald), 107.5 The Game, Yardbarker, beIN Sports and the Plain Text Sports play-by-play. All 124 Lakers points and all 114 Hawks points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals. Halftime was 68–57 and it was 95–90 after three (box score, 107.5 The Game, Yardbarker). Biggest leads: the Lakers' 20 and Atlanta's 8 (Covers.com); Atlanta led 19–11 early (107.5 The Game). Bench points (49–45) are summed from the box score. Dončić sat out Sunday's win at Detroit with low back tightness and returned for the second night of the back-to-back; Austin Reaves missed this game with an illness (AP, 107.5 The Game). The win was the Lakers' sixth straight and ended Atlanta's four-game winning streak (AP, 107.5 The Game). The Lakers are 10–2, first in the West, and play at Milwaukee on Wednesday at 8:00 PM ET (FOX Sports standings, Yardbarker). The Bucks' record is from the site's standings.

The play of the game is an original illustration of Luka Dončić's driving finger-roll layup with 2:27 left that made it 117–111 (Plain Text Sports play-by-play; the AP and 107.5 The Game also describe the layup). It came after Dyson Daniels' floater had cut the Lakers' lead to 115–111 with 3:30 left (AP), and Atlanta never got closer than six after it (107.5 The Game). It is drawn as a basket on a drive from 115–111; the finger-roll finish itself isn't animated. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Los Angeles Lakers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Dončić’s listed 6-foot-8 and 230 pounds (Basketball-Reference), with arms scaled to his reported 6-foot-11 wingspan (NBA Draft Room), in the Lakers' road kit. His No. 77 is from Basketball-Reference. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
